data.gist: Proposed but unverified mechanism: prior in vitro data (BMAX MSCs showing IRAP expression, higher IL-6 after TNF-α, lower IP-10, fewer leukocytes) may explain reduced pain and swelling, though these mediators were not measured here.
data.plain: The authors speculate that BMAX outperformed BMAC on movement-evoked pain and knee swelling because of differences in immune-signaling molecules released by the cells and in white blood cell content. In earlier in vitro work, BMAX-derived MSCs responded more strongly to the inflammatory cytokine TNF-α (expressing the IL-1 blocker IRAP and significantly more IL-6), while BMAC MSCs made much more of the leukocyte-attracting chemokine IP-10, likely because BMAC is overwhelmingly leukocytes. They explicitly state these mediators were not measured in the present study, so the mechanism remains speculative and needs future cytokine and molecular profiling.
